title: Global AI Pulse Q3 2026: AI at scale: Accountability, resilience and economics
date_basis: Publication imprint on page 30: September 2026; publication number 140611-G. No exact publication day established.
authorship_basis: Explicit Authors page (page 27), inspected visually and as text on 13 October 2026; names ordered left to right. Contributors and contacts on pages 28-29 are not substituted for authors.
summary: Online survey of 2,131 senior leaders: 89% report measurable AI value, while 12% consistently assess value against cost. Established ROI is reported by 10%; planned annual investment averages US$210 million. Management controls, accountability and provider resilience are associated with maturity.
limitations: Executive self-report in large organizations, not audited net returns or causal evidence. Value/cost questions exclude early-stage respondents; do not infer that 88% never evaluate value. Maturity includes self-reported ROI, so group comparisons are selection-sensitive. Wave changes do not establish within-firm improvement. KPMG sells related consulting services.
version_note: Q3 is a distinct quarterly wave, not the report underlying the June Q2 announcement. Fieldwork: 23 July-26 August 2026. Authors and contributors are separately identified. Selective AI-assisted synthesis/editorial work is disclosed on page 25. Commentary and survey findings are kept distinct.
verification_scope: Full 30-page publisher PDF; opening identity, author page 27, imprint page 30, methodology/definitions pages 25-26, findings and chart denominators pages 3-8, 11-13 and 16-22. Third-party PDF inspected locally, not redistributed.

document_verification.scope: Full report; named authors, publication imprint, survey scope and definitions, main findings, subgroup bases and value-versus-cost caveats.

title: Growing adoption signals progress as cost visibility and accountability drive AI value, new KPMG Global AI Pulse survey finds
summary: Q2 announcement describes 2,145 senior leaders surveyed in April-May 2026. Only 7% report established ROI; cost visibility and executive accountability correlate with reported returns. This is the earlier wave, not the September Q3 report.
limitations: Institutional summary and executive self-reports, not causal or audited evidence. Headline language about accountability driving results is stronger than the observational comparison establishes. Q2 and Q3 are related survey waves, not independent replications.
verification_scope: Full official announcement, Q2 report link, fieldwork/sample paragraph and quoted spokesperson blocks; Q2 PDF not separately inspected. Attribution retained from official press-release metadata.

title: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software
summary: Reports Chen and Stratton's firm-level study and its downstream review bottleneck.
limitations: Secondary coverage of an already included study, not independent evidence. The headline is stronger than a statistically insignificant output estimate warrants.
verification_scope: article text, byline and link to the author paper

title: The impact of AI on software engineers in 2026: key trends. Part 1
summary: A reader survey describes uneven benefits, rising costs, role changes and tensions between rapid delivery and maintenance.
limitations: Self-selected 900-plus responses; only the public preview was inspected. Editorial role categories are not a validated workforce taxonomy.
verification_scope: public introduction, reported sample size, key trends and subscription boundary; paid report not inspected

title: The risks of AI overreliance in software engineering
summary: Connects implementation gains with verification costs, code comprehension and long-term engineering capability.
limitations: Secondary synthesis, not a new experiment. The categorical productivity subheading is too broad; cited studies must be interpreted in their own settings.
verification_scope: article and linked primary studies; findings attributed to those studies

title: AI Is Eating Software and Investors Have Noticed
summary: Discusses delayed productivity effects and investors' expectations of AI-related software-sector change.
limitations: Market interpretation and forecasts, not a causal evaluation of AI deployment. Inspected the public text only, not subscriber functionality.
verification_scope: public article text, Bloomberg byline and publication date

title: The turbulent AI era is here. The choices we make now are critical.
title_aliases: The choices we make about AI now are critical
summary: Argues that AI's benefits and disruption require preparation, equitable access and protection for affected people.
limitations: A prominent technology stakeholder's argument and forecasts, not empirical proof of future reliability or aggregate welfare gains.
verification_scope: main essay and dated author block, excluding unrelated articles embedded on the page

title: The Impacts of Artificial Intelligence throughout the Software Development Life-cycle on Sustainability: A Mixed-method Study
container_title: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 10th International Workshop on Green and Sustainable Software
summary: Combines 64 studies with 27 interviews across 12 countries, identifying efficiency benefits alongside energy, dependency, skill and defect concerns.
limitations: Small, geographically concentrated interview sample; broad AI scope and literature through mid-2025. Qualitative findings do not quantify net environmental impact.
verification_scope: publisher full-text rendering, abstract, methodology and validity discussion

title: AI Writes Faster Than Humans Can Review: A Longitudinal Study of an Enterprise 2x Mandate
summary: One enterprise reaches 2.09 times baseline merged PRs per developer; review load also roughly doubles and automated review expands.
limitations: Nonrandom adoption and use, one AI-forward company and PR throughput rather than user value. Stable merge/revert rates do not establish absence of downstream defects.
version_note: Pinned to v1. Distinguish within-developer adoption estimates from the total organization-level throughput change.
verification_scope: version-specific abstract, panel scope, identification caveats and review findings

title: More Code, Less Understanding? On the Impact of AI Assistants on Developers' Productivity and Code Ownership
summary: Among 69 participants, AI improves median task completeness but reduces immediate correct answers about the code: 87.5% versus 100% without AI.
limitations: Mostly students; only 14 professionals. Short tasks and AI-generated comprehension questions do not measure permanent skill loss or long-run ownership.
version_note: Author-hosted manuscript; journal identity confirmed on the author's research page. The August 2021 running header is a LaTeX template artifact, not the publication date. DOI not yet established in this review.
verification_scope: author PDF abstract, participant table and study design; author publication list

title: Code provenance
summary: QEMU declines contributions containing or derived from AI-generated content because of provenance and Developer Certificate of Origin concerns; research and debugging assistance remain permitted if generated output is not submitted.
limitations: A policy and rationale, not a measured productivity effect or a definitive legal ruling. Live development documentation can change.
version_note: Policy observed on 13 October 2026; original adoption date not established.
verification_scope: official Use of AI-generated content section and its exceptions

title: AI Usage Policy
summary: Requires disclosure and human understanding of outside contributions, rejects generated media and sanctions low-quality submissions while explicitly welcoming responsible AI assistance.
limitations: Not a blanket AI-code ban or an experiment; maintainers have different permissions from external contributors.
version_note: Pinned to the latest file-changing revision available at the cutoff: 00c33eaf72af6c9b93d9fd8d54b6f7086612a95b, 15 February 2026.
verification_scope: official policy text, including scope and AI-is-welcome qualification; revision identity

title: Contributing to Ghostty
summary: First-time contributors require maintainer vouching; the project attributes the gate to low-quality submissions and erosion of default trust.
limitations: Shows an actual participation restriction, not its prevalence across open source or a causal estimate of AI harm.
verification_scope: official critical rule and first-time-contributor sections; revision identity

title: Math 2.0
summary: Proposes using AI to strengthen mathematical understanding, exposition and collaborative infrastructure rather than optimizing only the number of solved problems.
limitations: A research agenda and expert assessment, not a causal measurement of community health; examples include announced future activity.
version_note: Caltech lecture delivered 9 October; slides announced in Tao's blog on 10 October. Future November events are proposals, not completed outcomes.
verification_scope: 30-slide author PDF, especially capability, reporting-bias and human-understanding sections; linked author announcement

title: Terence Tao on AI in mathematics (and beyond)
summary: Connects Tao's evolving views, comparative advantage, verification and human-centered mathematics with primary writings and talks.
limitations: AI-drafted, reviewed and corrected by Tao; editorial selection and third-person paraphrase. Cite original works for specific arguments where possible.
version_note: Inspected version last updated 11 October 2026; page discloses AI assistance, industry access and collaborations.
verification_scope: authorship disclosure, update date, chronology and links to original works

title: Mathematics in the age of AI
summary: Asks what mathematical research is for, conditional on increasingly capable AI problem solving, rather than making a new capability estimate.
limitations: An ICM lecture-based conceptual argument; submission to proceedings does not establish peer review of this version.
verification_scope: version-specific arXiv abstract and bibliographic history

title: Mathematical methods and human thought in the age of AI
summary: Situates AI in the history of intellectual tools and argues for applications that expand human thought and meet human needs.
limitations: A philosophical framework, not a measured effect. Solicited chapter status is distinct from the unabridged preprint's publication status.
verification_scope: primary abstract, authorship and version history

title: A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics
summary: A declaration initiated by 25 Fields medallists recognizes stronger AI capabilities but opposes problem-count incentives disconnected from mathematical understanding.
limitations: Normative collective statement, not representative polling or an empirical estimate. Signatories are endorsers, not automatically bibliographic coauthors.
version_note: DOI is displayed by the official declaration and its preprint references; registration and landing-page access require separate automated checking.
verification_scope: official declaration text, date and Tao's dated explanation of initial signatories

title: AHM Statement on OpenAI's October 6 Release of Mathematical Documents
authors: Association for Human Mathematics Communications Working Group
summary: Rejects the value of OpenAI's mass mathematical release and calls for mathematicians to discontinue collaboration with the company.
limitations: A strong organizational position, not a vote of all mathematicians or a technical refutation of every released result. Legal allegations are not adjudicated here.
version_note: Date confirmed by the organization's text referring to the preceding day and Tao's 7 October guest repost. The official page contains multiple statements.
verification_scope: official statement and dated author-hosted repost; no claims drawn from blog comments

title: What mathematicians should know about the Lean Theorem Prover: questions of reliability and AI
summary: Separates kernel checking from statement fidelity, discusses independent checkers and soundness risks, and describes AI-assisted detection and repair of kernel bugs.
limitations: Expert technical account, not our independent execution of the proofs or a proof of complete kernel trustworthiness.
version_note: Guest author is Thomas Hales, not blog host Terence Tao. Formal checking and human exposition address different questions.
verification_scope: guest-authorship note and main reliability discussion; comments excluded

title: On the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
summary: Claims a solution of the forced Navier-Stokes breakdown alternatives, releasing a written proof and Lean formalization and describing a large multiagent effort.
limitations: Developer claim with unavailable internal model; announcement, formal checking, statement fidelity and prize recognition are separate evidentiary stages.
verification_scope: official announcement, result formulation, resource account and linked artifacts

title: Finite time blowup for Navier-Stokes
summary: The manuscript states a smooth forced flow with finite-time unbounded velocity and bounded kinetic energy, claiming the official breakdown alternatives.
limitations: Only the abstract, theorem statement and outline were inspected. This review does not independently validate the 166-page proof.
verification_scope: first-page theorem and proof outline, not all lemmas

title: Finite time blowup for Navier-Stokes and Euler equations
summary: Provides Lean formalization artifacts and independent-checking instructions accompanying the announced mathematical results.
limitations: Repository availability and build instructions are not our successful execution or an independent audit of formal statement fidelity.
version_note: Pinned to f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd, the revision examined by the October critique.
verification_scope: official README, artifact descriptions and revision identity; proof kernels not run

title: Navier-Stokes Announcement
summary: Welcomes the apparent resolution and anticipated new understanding while describing a deliberate evaluation process under the prize rules.
limitations: Not a prize award or an independent completed validation. Its September statement predates the October translation critique.
verification_scope: official dated statement and its qualification about evaluation

title: Navier-Stokes lost in translation: Why Lean verification of AI autoformalisation does not guarantee correct natural language proofs
summary: Identifies mismatches between OpenAI's written argument and Lean lemmas, distinguishing machine-checked validity from faithful translation.
limitations: A preprint critique, not a complete independent adjudication. Its worst-case ambiguity result is not proof that every practical autoformalization is impossible or that Lean's logic is invalid.
verification_scope: v1 abstract, concrete derivative-loss and estimate comparisons, and interpretation of translation limits; proofs not independently reproduced

title: Postmortem for the Kernel Soundness Bug Hunt
summary: The Lean maintainer documents AI-assisted discovery of soundness bugs and changes to proof-checking safeguards.
limitations: Maintainer-reported case, not a controlled security comparison. Finding and fixing bugs neither certifies a bug-free kernel nor invalidates all earlier formal proofs.
verification_scope: dated maintainer report and its distinction between builds and independent proof checking
